title: rate-envelope-controller-and-util-entropy-reporter
author: Nikhil Rao
description: Context: We currently rely on simple token-rate ceilings and percentile-based utilization for tenant throttling and autoscaler decisions. This leads to two operational gaps: 1) sudden bursty tenants can repeatedly cause short-lived tail latencies and capacity churn, and 2) our utilization signals (avg/p90) do not capture temporal volatility which is useful for preemptive autoscaling. Motivation: Introduce a lightweight runtime 'rate envelope' controller that enforces soft per-tenant concurrency/throughput envelopes with graceful degradation and backoff, and add a 'utilization entropy' reporter that quantifies temporal variability in per-tenant utilization to inform the autoscaler and the operations dashboard. High level changes: - New runtime controller pkg/autoscaler/rate_envelope_controller.go that enforces tenant envelopes and exposes a ranked violation metric. Envelope semantics are soft: requests that would exceed the envelope are accepted where possible but marked for best-effort throttling and may be routed to a lower-cost variant when SLA tier allows. - Utilization entropy reporter at pkg/telemetry/util_entropy_reporter.go that computes a rolling entropy-like score over time-bucketed utilization histograms (per-tenant, per-pool) and emits metrics util.entropy{tenant, pool} and util.entropy_percentile. - Autoscaler integration: the dedicated autoscaler now ingests util.entropy and uses a hysteresis-weighted scaling factor to favour scale-up on high-entropy tenants. Implementation notes and knobs: - rate_envelope is configurable via tenant config: envelope.max_concurrency, envelope.max_tokens_per_sec, envelope.penalty_backoff_ms. Defaults mimic current soft-burst limits but add a decay window. - util_entropy uses 1m buckets by default, 12-bucket rolling window (12 minutes), config at telem.entropy.window_size and telem.entropy.buckets. - A new admin API endpoint /admin/tenants/{id}/envelope lets SRE inspect and override envelopes for an incident. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated, default off for existing Dedicated customers. 2) Enable for a small pilot pool (canary) for 48h with increased telemetry retention. 3) Gradual ramp across remaining dedicated pools subject to per-pool validation. Tests and verification: - Unit tests for envelope admission, backoff penalty, and decay behavior. - Integration test that replays a bursty workload showing reduced tail latencies and fewer scale churn events. - Simulated autoscaler runs showing earlier scale-ups for high-entropy tenants and reduced oscillation. Backwards compatibility: Soft semantics preserve current behavior when feature disabled; metrics are additive. Related work: follows on ENG-4521 (tenant burst policy revamp) and ENG-4590 (autoscaler signal enrichment). See design doc: /docs/infra/rate-envelopes.md. Security: no new secrets; admin API requires existing admin RBAC.

b2d88e4: add util entropy reporter and metric exporter + tests

review_comments: Marina Chen: Nice model — can you explain why we chose entropy over variance? The design doc briefly mentions robustness to multi-modal patterns but I want a short justification in code comments.

Author (Nikhil Rao): Added inline comment in util_entropy_reporter.go explaining that entropy captures distribution shape and is less sensitive to single large outliers than variance; linked to a short note in the doc.
Luis Gomez: The admission path needs clearer telemetry for dropped vs penalized requests. Please emit envelope.admit{ok,penalized,dropped} counters and include the penalty reason label.
Author: Added counters and a small label set (reason: backpressure|variant-route|quota). Updated tests to assert counters.
Reza Haddad: Integration test shows a 12% reduction in tail latency for pilot. We should add a safety timeout to admin override to prevent accidental long-term overrides.
Author: Implemented admin override TTL with default 1h and updated API docs and console UI to show TTL.
release_notes: Introduce: rate envelope controller (soft per-tenant concurrency/throughput envelopes), util.entropy telemetry (temporal variability score) and autoscaler integration that uses entropy to reduce oscillation; Admin: new /admin/tenants/{id}/envelope override with TTL. Notes: feature gated for Dedicated; opt-in pilot followed by gradual rollout.
test_results_summary: Integration replay: p99 latency for pilot pool down 12% under same provision; autoscaler churn events reduced from 7->3 over 1h simulated window; CPU overhead ~0.6% in telemetry aggregator for 10k tenants.
notes_for_ops: When enabling on a pool: increase telemetry retention to 30m for entropy buckets during pilot, monitor metric util.entropy and envelope.admit_penalized. If penalized rates >5% sustained, inspect tenant workload and consider increasing envelope or routing policy.
